package_info.why_malicious: No specific malicious package is described in the report. The report discusses incident response and revocation strategies for compromised accounts and images in a Sigstore-enabled software supply chain, but does not analyze or present any particular malicious package or code. The focus is on the risks and detection of compromised signing identities and unauthorized image signatures.

behavioral_signatures: Unusual signing activity from a single identity (e.g., dev.a@example.com signing many images in a short period of time, which deviates from normal signing patterns).
Signatures for container images originating from accounts or identities not normally authorized to deploy or sign those images.

Presence of image signatures in the Sigstore transparency log (Rekor) for images that do not have corresponding entries in build logs or deployment records, indicating possible unauthorized or out-of-process signing.
file_indicators: Container images signed by accounts that have been identified as compromised or unauthorized.
Image digests (e.g., sha256:<digest>) associated with signatures from unexpected or unauthorized identities.
network_indicators: Signatures posted to the Sigstore transparency log (Rekor) from identities or IP addresses not normally associated with your organization's signing infrastructure.
Unusual or unauthorized access patterns to container registries or CI/CD systems, such as access from new locations or at atypical times.
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor Sigstore transparency logs for signatures issued by identities within your organization, with a focus on detecting anomalous activity such as unexpected images, high signing volume, or images not present in build or deployment logs. Cross-reference image digests found in the transparency log with your internal deployment and build records to identify unauthorized artifacts. Blocklist image digests associated with compromise. Monitor and enforce changes in allowed signers through admission controller policies to prevent deployment of images signed by unauthorized or compromised identities.
